name: Royal Danish Academy of Music
sector: institutioner inden for arkitektur og kunst
summary: Denmark's national classical music conservatory, in the former Radio House in Frederiksberg, Copenhagen. Its bachelor's in performance, church music, composition and Tonmeister are available in English. Entry is by audition only; the deadline is 1 December 2026, not 15 March.
about: A state music academy under the Ministry of Culture, offering three-year Bachelor of Music degrees in orchestral instruments, piano, guitar, accordion, voice, early music, organ, composition and sound engineering. Danish is its main working language, but it says every programme except Music Teaching is available in English. Places go by audition, not grades.

ib.text: No school-leaving qualification is required: an IB Diploma or DP Course Results both let you apply. Passing the January entrance exam in your principal study is the only requirement.

apply.via: Studieoptag, the Academy's own portal (not optagelse.dk)

dates.label: Piano-video set task and scales published
Applications close for every bachelor programme (12:00 noon)

languageOfInstruction.note: The Academy says every programme except Music Teaching is available in English, with principal-study teaching and exams in English. Danish remains its primary working language, and Music Teaching needs fluent Danish.

sources.title: Every programme except Music Teaching is available in English: principal-study teaching is in English and exams can be held in English. EU/EEA applicants are recommended an English level around IELTS 5.5; non-EU/EEA applicants must document it (IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 60 or LanguageCert B2, or English-medium schooling plus an interview).
sources.quote: To be successful in their studies at RDAM, we recommend EU/EEA students to have an English level equivalent to a score of 5.5 IELTS. [...] Non-EU/EEA applicants who wish to apply for a full degree study must provide documentation of a sufficient level of English language proficiency. [...] International students at RDAM can expect that information the students are provided in both English and Danish. Furthermore, all programmes, except the Music Teacher Programme, are available in English. Special arrangements with teachers are possible within these programmes. The main subject (principal subject) is conducted in English, and if needed, examinations are also held in English.

sources.title: RDAM language policy (August 2024): Danish is the primary language of instruction and work, communication takes place in Danish and English, and every student is expected to be able to receive instruction in English.
sources.quote: RDAM is a Danish educational institution, where the primary language of instruction and working language is Danish – but communication takes place in Danish and English. All students and staff are expected to be able to communicate in English. [...] All students – Danish and international – at RDAM are expected to be able to receive instruction in English.

sources.title: Completed upper-secondary school is not required. Danish is the Academy's primary language of instruction and work, with communication in Danish and English; EU/EEA citizens pay no tuition; entrance exams for bachelor applicants are mainly in January and February.
sources.quote: It is not a requirement to have completed upper secondary school or an equivalent education (e.g. highschool) in order to apply for admission to the Royal Danish Academy of Music. [...] RDAM is a Danish educational institution where the primary language of instruction and work is Danish – though communication occurs in both Danish and English. [...] There are no tuition fees for students with an EU/EEA citizenship.

notes: Bachelor applications close on 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon through Studieoptag; the 15 March optagelse.dk deadline does not apply, and the programmes are not in KOT, so there is no grade cut-off.
EU/EEA applicants audition in person in Copenhagen in January 2027; final answers come in mid-March. Applicants from outside the EU/EEA take an online entrance exam instead.
The bachelor's admission is coordinated between the Danish music academies: you audition only at your first choice, which can pass your application to a second academy you name.
Music Teaching (AM) is taught in Danish and needs fluent Danish, so it is not listed here.
The Academy offers no scholarships. EU applicants have no age limit; non-EU applicants must be 18 by 1 June 2027.

requirements.note: The entrance examination is the only requirement, so IB points and Course Results decide nothing. This is not an optagelse.dk programme and Denmark's quota rules do not apply.

sources.title: The only requirement for the Bachelor's programme is passing the Academy's entrance examination. There is no age limit for EU applicants; non-EU applicants must be 18 by 1 June of the application year; Swiss applicants apply as EU/EEA applicants. Admission rests mainly on the entrance exam, but the balance of instruments and voices can also decide.
sources.quote: To be admitted to the Bachelor's program, the only requirement is that you pass the entrance examination at the Academy. [...] All non-EU applicants must be 18 years old by 1 June of the year they apply for admission. Applicants from Switzerland apply for admission as EU/EEA applicants. Music academies typically cannot admit all qualified applicants. Admission is primarily based on the results of the entrance exam, but other factors may also be decisive, such as specific needs in the music world and the Academy's ability to create a balanced ensemble of instruments and voices for group performances, etc.

sources.title: Completed upper-secondary school is not required. Danish is the Academy's primary language of instruction and work, with communication in Danish and English; EU/EEA citizens pay no tuition; entrance exams for bachelor applicants are mainly in January and February.
sources.quote: It is not a requirement to have completed upper secondary school or an equivalent education (e.g. highschool) in order to apply for admission to the Royal Danish Academy of Music. [...] RDAM is a Danish educational institution where the primary language of instruction and work is Danish – though communication occurs in both Danish and English. [...] There are no tuition fees for students with an EU/EEA citizenship.

requirements.label: Written technical test, auditive analysis and discussion, then an aural and theory test; audiogram and piano video too

sources.title: Entrance examination for the Bachelor's programme for Tonmeister: a 60-minute written test of technical and musical knowledge, an auditive analysis of two recordings and a discussion, then the aural training and theory test; a basic-piano video and a certified audiogram (at most a year old) go with the application.

Every bachelor applicant who passes the principal-study audition takes a written aural training and theory test of about two and a half hours (EU/EEA). Most instrumentalists, singers and church musicians also submit a piano video with the application; piano, guitar, accordion and harpsichord applicants are exempt. The set piano task is published on 20 November 2026.
sources.quote: All EU/EEA applicants for Bachelor's programmes at the Academy who has passed an entrance examination in the principal study must take a written test in aural training and theory. Duration approx. 2 ½ hours. [...] most instrumentalists, singers, and church musicians (EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA) must take the entrance examination in piano as a supporting subject. [...] Piano, guitar, accordion, and harpsichord are exempted from the examination in piano as a supporting subject. [...] Set task: Available on 20 November 2026 at 10.00 AM

sources.title: Entrance examinations 2027 (updated 13 November 2026): in-person BMus auditions run from 4 to 28 January 2027 by principal study, followed by the aural training and theory test; harp and harpsichord dates are still to be announced.

requirements.label: Applicants outside the EU/EEA only: documented English, such as IELTS Academic 5.5 or TOEFL iBT 60
requirements.note: EU/EEA applicants document nothing; the Academy recommends an English level around IELTS 5.5.

sources.title: Every programme except Music Teaching is available in English: principal-study teaching is in English and exams can be held in English. EU/EEA applicants are recommended an English level around IELTS 5.5; non-EU/EEA applicants must document it (IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 60 or LanguageCert B2, or English-medium schooling plus an interview).
sources.quote: To be successful in their studies at RDAM, we recommend EU/EEA students to have an English level equivalent to a score of 5.5 IELTS. [...] Non-EU/EEA applicants who wish to apply for a full degree study must provide documentation of a sufficient level of English language proficiency. [...] International students at RDAM can expect that information the students are provided in both English and Danish. Furthermore, all programmes, except the Music Teacher Programme, are available in English. Special arrangements with teachers are possible within these programmes. The main subject (principal subject) is conducted in English, and if needed, examinations are also held in English.

sources.title: EU/EEA applicants apply on Studieoptag and pay DKK 500; bachelor applications open in mid-October; you can name a second Danish music academy in the coordinated bachelor admission; final answers come in mid-March; the academic year begins at the end of August.
sources.quote: Applications for admission to the Royal Danish Academy of Music are submitted through the application portal, Studieoptag, by filling out the application form and paying the application fee (500 DKK). Applications for Bachelor's and Master's programmes are open from mid-October [...] There is a coordinated application process for Bachelor's programmes at the Danish music academies. [...] We send final responses for all applications to the Bachelor's and Master's programmes in mid-March [...] The academic year always begins at the end of August.
